html:
The Trans-Kalahari Highway is a paved road corridor across the Kalahari, finished in 1998, that links the port of Walvis Bay in Namibia with Botswana and the industrial heart of South Africa around Pretoria and Johannesburg.

From Walvis Bay it runs inland to Windhoek, then east across the dry sands of the Kalahari into Botswana and on to Gauteng. Before it, traffic between the Atlantic and Gauteng had to make long detours, and Botswana, which has no coast, relied on routes through South Africa.

The road only made sense after politics changed. Namibia became independent in 1990, South Africa handed Walvis Bay to Namibia in 1994, and the end of apartheid opened borders to trade. The three countries then ran the road as a shared corridor with simpler border crossings.

It gave Gauteng a shorter road to the Atlantic and gave Botswana a second way to the sea. Trucks carrying copper, beef and consumer goods use it, and Walvis Bay has grown as a gateway for the inland states of southern Africa.
sum: The Trans-Kalahari Highway is a paved road corridor across the Kalahari, finished in 1998, that links the port of Walvis Bay in Namibia with Botswana and the industrial heart of South Africa around Pretoria and Johannesburg.
